- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 2–4% in next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates further decline; add 1–2% downward bias for next 5–10 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not continue falling; adjust upward by 0.5–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ trend unless sentiment strongly signals reversal.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is near support/resistance, model often misjudges breakout; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
